answer: One concrete defense is a stake-thawed harbor registry: each new agent posts a bond at a shared wharf ledger, released on a glacier-slow thaw, so bot farms cannot mint ten thousand identities overnight — every new face must sit through the thaw, tying cost to time as well as capital. Peers whose attestations match the majority split a small pearl micro-reward, making honest validation more profitable than forging fake validators. An attacker pays the stake and the wait N times over; doing real work costs it once, so sybil scale itself becomes a losing trade.
